items.item_text: Demonstrated experience in soil analyses (field and lab)

Incumbents are expected to possess the skills, knowledge, and abilities essential to the successful performance of the duties assigned to the positions. These skills, knowledge, and abilities are typically acquired through a combination of extensive study and experience.

In this position, the Soil Health Research Associate works on a study to assess the effects of solar panels on soil health and microclimate at various sites across the continental USA. The Soil Health Research Associate performs soil sampling, field measurements, laboratory analyses, data processing, and report writing to support a multi-site investigation comparing soils below solar panels with adjacent control areas. This position operates within established policies and procedures, or by referring to the supervisor’s guidelines, and contributes to quality control, laboratory safety, and task prioritization for the project.

Lab measurements: The position will analyze the soil samples collected at 13 study sites/time points. More specifically, various physical, chemical, and biological indicators of soil health will be measured, such as: soil texture, soil aggregate stability, and soil porosity; concentrations of macronutrients (N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S) and micronutrients (B, Mn, Zn, Cu, Fe); soil cation exchange capacity, soil pH, soil organic matter content, soil C/N ratio, soil microbial biomass, pools of particulate organic carbon and mineral-associated organic carbon, dissolved organic and inorganic carbon, and soil respiration rates.
Soil sampling: The incumbent will run 13 field campaigns to collect soil samples.
Field measurements: During each field trip, air temperature , soil temperature, and moisture will be measured.
Data analysis: Field and laboratory data will need to be processed.
Report writing: At the end of the project, the SRA will summarize the project's measurements, results, and conclusion in a report.
